name: Reverse Box Turn (backward half)
notes: Owner's description (2026-11-16): the Box Turn with everything reversed. Follows Reverse Box Turn (forward half); the lead starts back on the right foot, side on the left, close the right, turning a quarter to the left; no rise. Called the Left Box Turn in the American syllabus. Turn timing from the book (2026-11-17, a box-step study card: the partner going back, on the inside of the turn, "commences to turn" on 1, turns 1/4 between 1 and 2 with the "body turns less", and the body completes the turn on 3; the partner going forward turns 1/8 between 1 and 2 and 1/8 between 2 and 3). Written as the mirror image of Box Turn (backward half) (2026-11-17): the bodies turn 1/24 left on count 1, 1/8 on count 2 and 1/12 on the close; the lead, going back on the inside, points his count-2 foot a further 1/8; the close's turn is carried back into count 2's foot placement; the couple turns round the lead (the default turning centre). Provisional sizes, the same as the Box Turn's mirrored: count 1 0.4 back and 0.2 to his right, count 2 0.6 back and 0.3 right of where his left foot was. Before this change (0.5 back, then 0.9 back and 0.2 right, the whole quarter on count 2) the follow's count 2 was a 1.24 m stride that sank her hips 0.38-0.44 m; now at most 0.08 m, and every check passes.
